posts.name: Dandolo
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

I’m assuming Voss didn’t flip because Fixer had some enormous irreducible damage heading toward him. Going through all the Scions I’m surprised there weren’t more incaps.

Fixer managed to land a hit with Riveting Crane in play. Oblivaeon was on side 1 so there wasn’t much benefit to fighting him or other Scion so in the 1 round opening Fixer created I focused on Voss and did 30ish damage to him. The remaining damage came from Oblivaeon himself and Borr the unstable over the course of the destruction of both Tomb of Anubis and Rook City in the same turn (all heroes were present but immune thanks to True Hero in the end). That turn was the major turning point in the game since it eliminated all the Scions but left no backup environments and OnlivAeon gained 10 devastation tokens since no heroes took damage from Oblivaeon’s end of turn effect or the Oblivaeon Shield.

posts.name: Dandolo
posts.cooked:
Missingno:

Jeez, teams are sturggling with the sheild it seems.

Yeah, the major issue’s the teams have been facing are:
-The extra Aeonmen mean more Aeon locus will be destroyed and mean more OblivAeon deck plays. This led to me seeing Temporal Fractures every game giving me 1 less round.
-The ordering of Oblivaeon’s start of turn effects are super inconvenient. First the countdown ticks down (so even if you’ve cleared the Aeonmen with a round to spare you will still fail. Second the Shield is checked. Third the environment destruction occurs (meaning if Aeon Master is defeated this way you already missed the timing for the shield check). At the end of his turn Oblivaeon will play more Aeonmen in both zones so its tough to get another chance.
